newsitem.title: CANADA: Inco to buy nickel on market during dispute.
newsitem.headline: Inco to buy nickel on market during dispute.

text.p: Inco Ltd said on Monday it will keep customers supplied during the current lockout at its Thompson facility by using output from other Inco operations and by buying nickel on the open market.
"We will be discussing with our customers possible alternative products, both Inco-sourced and purchased," Inco spokesman Dan McSweeney said in a phone interview.
Inco locked out almost 1,400 union workers on Sunday night after they voted to reject Inco's final contract offer.
Inco produces about 100 million pounds of nickel a year from the Thompson area in northern Manitoba.
Inco makes regular purchases of nickel from the market, traders and other nickel producers, he said.
But the company has always complained it makes no profit from those purchases.
Last year, Inco had to buy 197 million pounds of nickel to meet demand.
The Thompson division produces about 5.6 percent of the Western world's supply of nickel, said mining analyst Ray Goldie.
The nickel market can probably work smoothly for about two weeks without production from Thompson, he said. After two weeks, the nickel price will likely start to react, he added.
But shareholders seem to like the lockout, Goldie said.
Shares were up C$0.20 to C$43.35 in trading of 1.1 million shares by mid-afternoon.
Investors "seem to think that what they lose in volume, they would make up in price," Goldie said.
